observation.visible_scene: A daytime sky dominated by a flat layer of grey-blue cloud. The sun is hidden just behind the cloud edge at right-of-center, producing a bright glowing patch and a fan of crepuscular rays streaming downward and to the right; fainter rays also spill to the left. A horizontal band of cloud with brightly backlit (silver-lined) edges crosses the middle of the frame, and a smaller lit cloud patch sits at the lower left. The upper sky is a smooth, featureless blue-grey.
visible_changes: The overall composition stays fixed across the excerpt: the bright sun-edge, the horizontal lit cloud band, the lower-left lit patch, and the fan of rays remain in the same pixel positions, indicating no detectable cloud translation and no camera pan or zoom.

Only very subtle, low-amplitude shimmering/variation in the brightness and crispness of the rays and the cloud-edge highlights occurs between frames; no ray grows, moves, or disappears as a discrete event.
No object enters, exits, occludes, or deforms in a way that is resolvable within this ~2.7 s window.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the clouds drift measurably over a longer timescale than shown.
Whether the sun's altitude or the ray geometry changes (e.g., a progressing sunset) outside this crop.
Whether the camera is truly locked or on a tripod versus drifting imperceptibly; the short, feature-poor background gives no strong parallax evidence.
uncertain_details: The minute frame-to-frame brightness fluctuations in the rays cannot be confidently attributed to real atmospheric flicker versus video compression noise.
Any extremely slow cloud motion would be below the resolution of this brief, near-static excerpt.
